title: The Ram Mandir Donation Scandal Has Reached ₹200 Crore. Eight Are in Jail. Fifty More Are Under the Scanner.
excerpt: CCTV caught temple staff skimming cash from donation boxes. Investigators found a 70-room hostel, luxury cars, and a paper trail that may stretch far beyond the eight arrests.
body:
India's most politically charged religious site is now at the centre of an equally charged financial scandal. Eight employees of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust have been arrested for allegedly embezzling donations from the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, and investigators believe the total amount siphoned could exceed ₹200 crore.

The arrests, made in late June after CCTV footage caught staff skimming cash from donation boxes, have sent shockwaves through a temple administration that oversees one of India's most generously funded religious institutions. A court in Ayodhya remanded all eight to 14 days of judicial custody. Police raids on their residences turned up nearly ₹2 crore in cash, luxury vehicles, land holdings, and other assets that far exceeded their modest incomes.

## How the Scheme Worked

The alleged fraud was strikingly simple. Cash collected from 14 donation boxes placed near the Ram Lalla sanctum sanctorum and along the darshan route was taken to a secure "confidential room" for counting. According to Mahipal Singh, the former head of accounts who has made explosive insider disclosures, counting staff would tally ₹12 lakh but record only ₹9–10 lakh on the voucher, pocketing the difference. When Singh raised the discrepancy — once finding ₹5 lakh in excess of the recorded amount in a single cash box — he was summarily removed from the counting process. Seven to eight months of CCTV footage was then deleted.

Around 50 employees were involved in the counting and verification process: 24 note-counting staff hired through a private agency at roughly ₹14,500 per month, 12 Trust employees as supervisors, and 14 officials from the State Bank of India and TCS serving as auditors. The scale of the operation raises uncomfortable questions about oversight at a temple that receives 1 to 1.5 lakh devotees daily.

## Sudden Wealth Under the Microscope

The most damning evidence has been the dramatic lifestyle changes among the accused. Ramshankar Yadav, known locally as "Tinnu," was once an auto-rickshaw driver. Investigators are now scrutinising assets allegedly worth ₹50 crore linked to him, including a 70-room hostel near Ayodhya airport, stakes in three restaurants, a Toyota Fortuner, and properties in both Ayodhya and Lucknow. Another accused, Lavkush, was a car mechanic before joining the temple staff; police recovered ₹10 lakh in cash from his residence and discovered a house under construction in Faizabad.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who belongs to the BJP that built its national prominence partly on the temple's construction, has warned that those involved will "face the consequences." The state government has constituted a Special Investigation Team headed by Lucknow's Divisional Commissioner, with an IPS officer who previously served in the CBI and a senior Finance Department official. A senior IPS officer was also flown in from Delhi to prepare a report.

## Legal and Political Fallout

The scandal has already crossed into the courts. A Public Interest Litigation filed before the Allahabad High Court seeks a CBI investigation and a full forensic audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General. The petitioner argues that the Trust's initial posture of "institutional denial" — its spokesperson dismissed early reports as "mere rumours" — makes an independent probe urgently necessary.

Politically, the embarrassment is acute. The Ram Mandir was consecrated by Prime Minister Modi in January 2024 after decades of legal battles and was funded primarily by donations from devotees across India and the global diaspora. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has seized on the scandal, and what began as a local Ayodhya controversy has escalated into a national story.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

Millions of NRIs contributed to the temple's construction fund during a nationwide donation drive. For many, the Ram Mandir represented something beyond a religious structure — it was a symbol of cultural identity and a tangible connection to India. The revelation that temple staff may have been systematically stealing from donation boxes undermines that trust. The SIT has been asked to submit its findings within 15 days, and whether the investigation leads to deeper accountability or stays limited to mid-level staff will be closely watched — in Ayodhya and abroad.
